q: For a goods performance review, a railway has to report the tonnes actually unloaded at its own stations, including the traffic it received from other railways for delivery. In goods statistics, this figure is the:

options.C: Tonnes handed over by the railway to other railways
options.D: Tonnes transhipped at break-of-gauge points of the railway

e: Tonnes terminating are the tonnes actually unloaded and delivered at stations of a railway, including traffic received from other railways for termination on it.

q: A probationer writing a note on railway information systems has to expand the abbreviation CRIS correctly. CRIS stands for:
e: CRIS stands for Centre for Railway Information Systems, the organisation that develops and maintains the major information systems of Indian Railways.

q: The goods tariff and the conference rules under which freight rating works are issued under the authority of the body abbreviated as IRCA, which stands for:
e: IRCA stands for Indian Railway Conference Association, the body under whose authority the goods tariff and conference rules for rating and carriage are issued.

q: A lady passenger travelling alone with a young child asks about the special reserved accommodation earmarked for passengers like her. The Ladies Quota in trains is earmarked for allotment to:

options.A: Lady passengers travelling alone or with young children, in the trains and classes in which the quota is provided
options.B: Female railway employees travelling on duty only
options.C: Women members of the families of railway staff only
options.D: Holders of free complimentary passes only

e: The Ladies Quota is earmarked for lady passengers travelling alone or with young children, in the trains and classes in which that quota is provided.

q: Passengers booked for a branch-line town remain seated in their coach at the junction, and the coach itself is detached and attached to a connecting train for their destination. This arrangement is known as a:
e: A slip coach is a coach detached at a junction and attached to a connecting train for its destination, so its passengers travel through without changing coaches.

q: A statistics clerk compiling vehicle-kilometre figures looks for the guard's document that lists the vehicles composing each train. That basic record is the:
e: The Vehicle Guidance, prepared by the guard, lists the vehicles composing each train in order and is the basic record from which vehicle kilometres are compiled.

q: A freight customer tracing his consignment on the system quotes the number allotted to it at the time of booking through the Freight Operations Information System. This number, abbreviated as FNR, stands for:
e: FNR stands for Freight Name Record. It is the number allotted at booking through the Freight Operations Information System, by which a freight consignment is identified and traced.

q: A visitor holding a platform ticket demands that he be allowed to board an unreserved coach to see off a relative travelling in it. The correct position is that a platform ticket authorises the holder only to:

options.A: Enter the station platform for the period of its validity, and does not authorise him to travel by any train
options.B: Travel in the unreserved coach of any train leaving the station
options.C: Occupy a seat in the waiting room for twenty-four hours
options.D: Book luggage at the parcel office at concessional rates

e: A platform ticket authorises the holder only to enter the station platform for the period of its validity. It never authorises travel by any train.

q: A daily commuter observes that his Monthly Season Ticket costs him far less than the fares of all the journeys he makes on it during the month. This is because the fare of a Monthly Season Ticket is fixed as:

options.A: The fare for thirty single journeys at full rates
options.B: The Tatkal premium fare for the section
options.C: The fare of a single return journey in the same class
options.D: A highly concessional multiple-journey fare, far below the aggregate of the single-journey fares for the journeys it permits

e: A Monthly Season Ticket is priced as a highly concessional multiple-journey fare, far below the total of single-journey fares for all the journeys it permits in the month.

q: In the traffic Cash Office, an official is present specifically to witness the counting of cash remitted by stations and the acknowledgement given for it, the acknowledgement foil being returned to the station. This official is the:
e: The Cash Witness is the official who witnesses counting of station cash remittances in the Cash Office and the acknowledgement given for them, whose foil returns to the station.

q: Passengers boarding at several intermediate stations of a train draw their reserved accommodation from one common quota shared by those stations. Such a quota is known as the:
e: A quota of reserved accommodation shared in common by passengers boarding at several intermediate stations is called the Pooled Quota.

q: The statement which a station renders every day, showing the traffic cash it collected that day and how that cash was remitted or disposed of, is the:
e: The Daily Traffic Cash Statement is rendered daily by a station, showing the traffic cash collected that day and how it was remitted or otherwise disposed of.

q: In judging the punctuality of passenger trains, a train which reaches its destination without losing time en route as compared with its booked timings is described as:
e: In punctuality statistics a train that reaches its destination without losing time en route against its booked timings is described as not losing time.

q: A large party of pilgrims wants reserved accommodation together in one train, far beyond the number that can be booked on an ordinary requisition form. Such reservation is arranged as:

options.A: A current reservation at the station of departure
options.B: A booking made only through licensed travel agents
options.C: A bulk or group booking, on application to the competent reservation authority under the prescribed conditions
options.D: A set of separate Tatkal bookings made by the group leader

e: Reservation for a large party beyond an ordinary requisition is arranged as a bulk or group booking, on application to the competent reservation authority under the prescribed conditions.

q: A horse owner books his horses for carriage by rail and is told they will not be loaded in an ordinary goods wagon. Horses booked for carriage by rail are carried in:

options.A: Horse boxes, being the special vehicles provided for the carriage of horses
options.B: Ordinary open wagons used for goods traffic
options.C: Parcel vans, along with the parcel traffic
options.D: The brake van of a passenger train in every case

e: Horses are carried in horse boxes, the special vehicles provided for their carriage, and not in ordinary goods wagons or parcel vans.

q: Traders are licensed plots of railway land next to a goods shed for stacking and storing their consignments in connection with traffic moved by rail. Such licensed land is referred to as a:
e: Railway land licensed to traders beside a goods shed for stacking and storing consignments connected with rail traffic is called a commercial plot.

q: A Divyangjan passenger at a major station asks for a wheelchair to reach his coach and is told no charge will be made for it. The wheelchair facility at major stations is made available:

options.A: On payment of hire charges in every case
options.B: Only to passengers holding reserved tickets, on payment
options.C: Only against a refundable security deposit

e: Wheelchair facility at major stations is provided free of charge to passengers who need it, and no hire charge or security deposit is taken for it.

q: Two stations are compared for the passenger amenities to be provided at them, and one is placed in a higher category than the other. Stations are categorised for this purpose, in categories such as NSG, SG and HG, primarily on the basis of:

options.A: The age of the station building
options.B: The earnings of the station and the number of passengers dealt with at it
options.C: The number of platforms at the station only
options.D: The staff strength sanctioned for the station

e: Stations are categorised as NSG, SG and HG for passenger amenities primarily on the basis of station earnings and the number of passengers dealt with at the station.

q: A man enters a carriage to travel, saying he will buy his ticket from the ticket examiner on the train. Under Section 55 of the Railways Act, 1989, the correct position is that:

options.A: A passenger may travel without a ticket provided he pays the fare at the destination station
options.B: No person is entitled to enter or remain in a carriage for the purpose of travelling as a passenger unless he has with him a proper pass or ticket
options.C: A ticket is required only for journeys in reserved coaches
options.D: A season ticket holder requires no ticket or pass of any kind

e: Section 55 of the Railways Act, 1989 provides that no person is entitled to enter or remain in a carriage for travelling unless he has with him a proper pass or ticket.

q: A passenger in a running train needs to alert the railway servant in charge of the train in an emergency. Section 59 of the Railways Act, 1989 requires every railway administration to provide:

options.A: Efficient means of communication between the passengers and the railway servant in charge of the train
options.B: A complaint book in every reserved coach of the train
options.C: A public address system at every halt station
options.D: Telephone facilities in the brake van of every goods train

e: Section 59 of the Railways Act, 1989 requires every railway administration to provide efficient means of communication between passengers and the railway servant in charge of the train.

q: The time allowed to parties for loading or unloading wagons and for delivering or removing goods is fixed by the railway administration under:
e: Section 95 of the Railways Act, 1989 empowers the railway administration to fix the time allowed for loading or unloading wagons and for delivering or removing goods.

q: A railway administration reserves certain compartments and seats in a train for the exclusive use of female passengers. The power to earmark accommodation in this manner flows from:
e: Section 58 of the Railways Act, 1989 empowers the railway administration to earmark compartments, berths or seats in a train for the exclusive use of female passengers.

q: In a dispute about the weight of a consignment, the Railways rely on the Railway Receipt as evidence. Under Section 65 of the Railways Act, 1989, a Railway Receipt serves as prima facie evidence of:

options.A: The weight and the number of packages stated in it, subject to the endorsements made on it
options.B: The market value of the goods booked under it
options.C: The ownership of the goods by the Railways
options.D: The condition of the goods at the time of delivery

e: Under Section 65 of the Railways Act, 1989, a Railway Receipt is prima facie evidence of the weight and number of packages stated in it, subject to its endorsements.

q: During a surprise check of a station, the cash physically found is more than the balance shown in the station accounts. The excess amount so found is:

options.A: Retained by the Station Master for meeting petty expenses
options.B: Credited to the account of the Railways and brought into the accounts, the matter being reported for investigation
options.C: Distributed among the booking staff of the station
options.D: Treated as the personal money of the cashier and returned to him

e: Cash found in excess at a surprise check is railway money until proved otherwise. It is credited to the Railways and brought into account, and the matter is reported for investigation.

q: A consignee comes to the parcel office at the destination to collect a parcel booked to him. Delivery of the parcel is normally given to him:

options.A: On a verbal identification of the parcel by its description
options.B: Only after the expiry of the free time allowed for parcels
options.C: On surrender of the Parcel Way Bill by the consignee or his endorsee
options.D: Only on production of the forwarding station's balance sheet

e: A parcel is delivered only against its authority document. Delivery is given to the consignee or his endorsee on surrender of the Parcel Way Bill at the destination.

q: Articles left behind by passengers are deposited in the Lost Property Office, but some remain unclaimed even after the prescribed period. Such unclaimed articles are then:

options.A: Handed over free of charge to the person who found them
options.B: Destroyed by the station staff without any record
options.C: Retained in the office indefinitely at no charge
options.D: Disposed of by public auction, the sale proceeds being credited to the Railways if the owner is not traced

e: Unclaimed articles in the Lost Property Office, after the prescribed period and if the owner is not traced, are disposed of by public auction and the proceeds credited to the Railways.

q: A waitlisted passenger who had opted for the facility at booking finds, on preparation of the chart, that he has been given a berth in a higher class without paying anything extra. This has happened under the:
e: Under the Auto Upgradation Scheme, a waitlisted passenger who opted for it may be allotted accommodation in a higher class at charting without paying any extra charges.

q: Five passengers are booked under a single PNR and one of them drops out before the journey, while the other four still wish to travel. In this situation:

options.A: The entire PNR must be cancelled and a fresh booking made for the remaining passengers
options.B: The booking of the individual passenger can be cancelled separately, the reservation of the remaining passengers continuing under the same PNR
options.C: Partial cancellation of a PNR is not permitted under any circumstances
options.D: The fare of the passenger who drops out is forfeited in full in every case

e: Partial cancellation is permitted on a PNR. The booking of the passenger who drops out can be cancelled separately, while the others continue under the same PNR.

q: A passenger pays a licensed porter at the station for carrying his luggage to the train. In regard to this payment, the correct position is that the porter's charges:

options.A: Form part of the coaching earnings of the Railways
options.B: Are collected by the Railways and paid to the porters as wages
options.C: Are paid by the passengers directly to the porters and do not form part of the earnings of the Railways
options.D: Form part of the sundry other earnings of the Railways

e: Licensed porters are not railway employees paid from earnings. Their charges are paid by passengers directly to the porters and do not form part of railway earnings.

q: Blank Paper Ticket books supplied to a station are not treated like ordinary printed forms, because the tickets in them are issued to the public against payment. Such books are treated as:

options.B: Books supplied without any indent from the station
options.C: Books which are destroyed after use without any accountal
options.D: Money-value books, whose accountal is watched in the Traffic Accounts Office

e: Blank Paper Ticket books are money-value books, because their tickets are sold for money. Their accountal is therefore watched in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: A control office watches whether running staff are being given their due rest and are not worked beyond their hours of duty, using the data of the system in which the staff are booked and rostered. That system is the:
e: The Crew Management System is the system in which running staff are booked, rostered and monitored, so that their rest and hours of duty can be watched by control.

q: At a parcel office working on the Parcel Management System, the booking of a parcel is done through the system itself. On such booking, the system:

options.A: Is used only for printing the Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Is used only for the allotment of parcel vans to trains
options.C: Is used only for recording the attendance of parcel staff
options.D: Generates the Parcel Way Bill and computes the charges payable on the parcel

e: On booking through the Parcel Management System, the system itself generates the Parcel Way Bill and computes the charges payable on the parcel.

q: The holder of a parking contract at a station persistently defaults in paying the licence fee due to the Railways despite reminders. Under the terms of such an earning contract:

options.A: The contract continues indefinitely and no action can be taken on the security deposit
options.B: The security deposit held for the contract is liable to be forfeited and the contract is liable to be terminated
options.C: The dues are recovered from the salary of the Station Master
options.D: The dues are written off by the station as a matter of course

e: On persistent default in licence fee, the earning contract terms make the security deposit liable to forfeiture and the contract itself liable to termination.

q: A claimant who has won compensation before the Railway Claims Tribunal asks how the Tribunal's order in his favour can be enforced. An order of the Tribunal awarding compensation is:

options.A: Executable in the same manner as a decree of a civil court
options.B: Only advisory in nature and cannot be enforced
options.C: Enforceable only through a fresh suit in a civil court
options.D: Executable only after it is confirmed by the Railway Board

e: An order of the Railway Claims Tribunal awarding compensation is executable in the same manner as a decree of a civil court, and needs no fresh suit or Board confirmation.

q:
A wagonload consignment is accepted at a forwarding station which has no weighbridge, and its weight has somehow to be ascertained for charging freight. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. Where there is no weighbridge at the forwarding station, a wagonload consignment is weighed at the first available weighbridge en route.
2. The freight on such a consignment is accounted for on the weight so ascertained at the en-route weighbridge.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A wagonload from a station without a weighbridge is weighed at the first available weighbridge en route, and freight is accounted on that ascertained weight. Both statements are correct.

q: A consignor who has prepaid the freight withdraws his consignment before it is despatched from the forwarding station. The prepaid freight in such a case is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in full in all cases
options.B: Adjusted against the demurrage of other consignors at the station
options.C: Credited to the sundry earnings of the station
options.D: Refunded to the consignor after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charges

e: Prepaid freight on a consignment withdrawn before despatch is not forfeited. It is refunded to the consignor after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charges.

q: During his inspection of a station, the Travelling Inspector of Accounts notices several irregularities in its working and accounts. These irregularities are:

options.A: Noted by him personally and closed without any report to any office
options.B: Reported only to the statutory audit party after the close of the year
options.C: Communicated to the station for compliance, and their clearance is watched by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: Adjusted by him on the spot by altering the station accounts himself

e: Irregularities noticed by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts are communicated to the station for compliance, and their clearance is watched by the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: At a goods terminal working on the Terminal Management System of FOIS, no clerk works out the demurrage on detained wagons by hand at the end of the month. At such a terminal, the demurrage payable on wagons is:

options.A: Estimated by the goods clerk at the end of the month
options.B: Waived in all cases where the terminal is computerised
options.C: Charged at a flat rate for all wagons irrespective of the period of detention
options.D: Computed by the system from the placement and removal or release particulars of the wagons recorded in it

e: At a terminal on the Terminal Management System, demurrage is computed by the system itself from the recorded placement and removal or release particulars of the wagons.

q: A person presents himself at a booking office, pays the fare for his journey and demands a ticket for it. Under Section 50 of the Railways Act, 1989:

options.A: A railway administration may refuse to issue a ticket to any person without assigning a reason
options.B: Tickets can be issued only at the station from which the journey commences
options.C: A person desirous of travelling on the railway is entitled, on payment of the fare, to be supplied with a ticket by the railway administration
options.D: A ticket once issued can be transferred freely to any other person

e: Section 50 of the Railways Act, 1989 entitles a person desirous of travelling, on payment of the fare, to be supplied with a ticket by the railway administration.

q: Two zonal railways have interchanged a large volume of traffic with each other during a month, and their mutual dues for that traffic have now to be settled. Such settlements between zonal railways are effected:

options.A: In cash, by the Station Masters of the junction stations every day
options.B: Only at the close of the financial year, by the Railway Board in cash
options.C: By the consignors and passengers travelling over both the railways
options.D: Through the apportionment and transfer adjustments in the accounts of the railways concerned, on the basis of the interchange and invoice abstracts exchanged between them

e: Inter-railway dues are settled through apportionment and transfer adjustments in the accounts, based on the interchange and invoice abstracts exchanged between the railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross Tonne Kilometres are worked out after including the tare weight of the vehicles in the load hauled.
2. Net Tonne Kilometres are worked out after excluding the tare weight of the vehicles from the load hauled.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Gross Tonne Kilometres include the tare weight of vehicles in the load hauled, while Net Tonne Kilometres exclude tare and cover only the paying load. Both statements are correct.

q: During internal check, the Traffic Accounts Office notices that a merchant was made to pay freight in excess of the amount properly due from him, and the excess has to be returned. The document prepared for giving effect to this refund is the:
e: An overcharge sheet is the document prepared to refund freight charged in excess of the amount properly due, as detected during internal check in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: For watching the trend of railway earnings while the year is in progress, a statement of approximate gross earnings of Indian Railways is compiled and issued at an interval of:
e: A statement of approximate gross earnings of Indian Railways is compiled and issued every 10 days, so that the trend of earnings can be watched while the year is in progress.

q: A through consignment is carried partly over the home railway and partly over a neighbouring railway. The home railway is eventually credited, not with the whole amount collected at booking, but with its share worked out on the basis of the distance the traffic was carried over its own system. Such a share is known as its:
e: Apportioned earnings are a railway share of through traffic earnings, worked out on the basis of the distance the traffic was carried over its own system.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wharfage is the charge levied for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed for loading or unloading them.
2. Demurrage is the charge levied for goods not removed from the station premises within the free time allowed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements reverse the charges. Demurrage is for detention of wagons beyond free time, and wharfage is for goods not removed from station premises in time. Hence neither is correct.

q: Leakage of railway revenue at stations is sought to be prevented, among other measures, through inspections carried out at the stations themselves. The official who primarily performs this inspection function is the:
e: The Travelling Inspector of Accounts primarily performs inspections at stations, which is one of the measures to prevent leakage of railway revenue at stations.

q: A bundle of tickets sent back by a station as not having been issued is examined in the Traffic Accounts Office. The main object of this examination is to make sure that:

options.A: The fare printed on each ticket is the latest fare in force
options.B: The ticket stock register of the station is neatly maintained
options.C: The tickets returned as non-issued were in fact never sold or issued to passengers
options.D: The printing on the tickets is clear and legible

e: Non-issued tickets returned by a station are examined in the Traffic Accounts Office to make sure they were in fact never sold or issued to passengers.

q: At the end of a month, a station has collected its earnings and sent the remittance, but the amount has not yet been credited to the Railway's bank account. In traffic accounts, money in this situation is described as:
e: Earnings collected and remitted by a station but not yet credited to the Railway bank account are shown as Cash-in-Transit in traffic accounts.

q: A probationer suggests that the Traffic Accounts Office checks only a small percentage of the transactions in the accounts rendered by stations. The correct position is that the internal check exercised by that office is:

options.A: A detailed, cent per cent check of the accounts rendered
options.B: A test check confined to cash remittances only
options.C: A check exercised by the statutory audit party
options.D: A check confined to a small sample of transactions

e: The internal check exercised by the Traffic Accounts Office over station accounts is a detailed, cent per cent check of the accounts rendered, not a small sample check.

q: Unlike the balance sheet which each station prepares for its own transactions, the Accounts Office Balance Sheet in traffic accounts is prepared:

options.A: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection
options.B: By the Railway Board for all zonal railways together
options.C: By every station for the transactions of its division
options.D: In the Traffic Accounts Office, reflecting the position of station balances as per the accounts office books

e: The Accounts Office Balance Sheet is prepared in the Traffic Accounts Office and reflects the position of station balances as per the accounts office books.

q: A goods performance review requires one figure showing how far, on an average, each tonne of goods traffic was carried over the railway. This average lead of goods traffic is obtained by dividing:

options.A: Gross Tonne Kilometres by wagon kilometres
options.B: Net Tonne Kilometres by the tonnes carried
options.C: Train kilometres by the number of trains run
options.D: Goods earnings by the tonnes carried

e: Average lead of goods traffic is the average distance each tonne is carried. It is obtained by dividing Net Tonne Kilometres performed by the tonnes carried.

q: A diesel locomotive shed reports how much fuel its locomotives consume in relation to the work performed by them. Specific Fuel Consumption on Indian Railways is expressed per:
e: Specific Fuel Consumption of diesel locomotives is expressed per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres, relating fuel consumed to the gross work performed.

q: For electric traction, the electrical energy consumed is related to the work performed through Specific Energy Consumption, which is expressed as the energy consumed per:
e: Specific Energy Consumption for electric traction is the electrical energy consumed per 1000 Gross Tonne Kilometres of work performed.

q: Which of the following receipts does NOT belong to the category of sundry other earnings of the Railways?
e: Passenger fares are coaching earnings, not sundry other earnings. Sundry earnings cover items like advertisements, catering licence fees and commercial publicity.

q: The gross traffic earnings of a railway are made up of:

options.A: Coaching earnings and goods earnings only
options.B: Coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings
options.C: Goods earnings and parcel earnings only
options.D: Coaching earnings and sundry other earnings only

e: Gross traffic earnings comprise coaching earnings, goods earnings and sundry other earnings. These three heads together make up the total traffic earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements about earnings collected at a station:
1. Station earnings must be remitted in full and cannot be appropriated for meeting departmental expenditure at the station.
2. Petty station expenses may be met by the station out of the earnings collected by it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Station earnings must be remitted in full and cannot be appropriated for departmental expenditure, which is met from imprest. Only statement 1 is correct.

q: In certain premium trains, the fare charged from passengers rises or falls with the level of occupancy of the train under a system of dynamic pricing. This flexi fare system was introduced in:
e: The flexi fare system of dynamic pricing linked to occupancy was introduced in the premium Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Duronto trains, not in all trains.

q: Unreserved tickets are also sold by authorised agents working from premises outside the station, so that passengers need not come to the station merely to buy a ticket. In this connection, the abbreviation JTBS stands for:
e: JTBS stands for Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak, the authorised agents who sell unreserved tickets from premises outside station premises.

q: A booking clerk applies a fare lower than the fare properly chargeable for a journey, so that the passenger pays less than the amount actually due. In station accounts, such a case is one of:
e: Charging a fare lower than the fare properly chargeable, so the passenger pays less than due, is an undercharge in station accounts, as distinct from an overcharge.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Earnings of a period are the amounts that have accrued for the services rendered during that period, whether they have actually been received or not.
2. Revenue represents the earnings actually realised or received.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Earnings are amounts accrued for services rendered in a period, whether received or not, while revenue is the earnings actually realised or received. Both statements are correct.

q: Earnings of through traffic are divided among the railways which carried the traffic. Which of the following categories of earnings is NOT so apportioned?
e: Sundry other earnings are local earnings of the earning railway and are not divided. Coaching, goods and parcel earnings of through traffic are apportioned among the carrying railways.

q: Money earned by carrying parcels, luggage and postal traffic by trains is not shown under goods earnings or sundry earnings. On Indian Railways, such earnings are classified under:
e: Earnings from parcels, luggage and postal traffic are classified under other coaching earnings, and not under goods earnings or sundry other earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Advice of Internal Check:
1. It is prepared separately for coaching accounts and for goods accounts.
2. It is issued before the station balance sheet is received in the Traffic Accounts Office for check.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Advice of Internal Check is prepared separately for coaching and goods accounts, but it is issued only after the station balance sheet is received and checked. Only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the modules of the Freight Operations Information System:
1. RMS stands for Rake Management System.
2. TMS stands for Terminal Management System.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In FOIS, RMS stands for Rake Management System and TMS stands for Terminal Management System. Both statements are correct.

q: Reservations at computerised counters all over the country are made through the Passenger Reservation System. The computer software on which this system operates is known as:
e: CONCERT is the software on which the Passenger Reservation System operates for computerised reservations at counters all over the country.

q: Large railway information systems such as the Passenger Reservation System and the Freight Operations Information System have been developed, and are maintained, by:

options.B: Rail India Technical and Economic Service (RITES)
options.C: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)

e: Large systems like the Passenger Reservation System and FOIS have been developed and are maintained by the Centre for Railway Information Systems, or CRIS.

q: A passenger checks the running position of his train through the national enquiry facility provided for the purpose. In this connection, the abbreviation NTES stands for:
e: NTES stands for National Train Enquiry System, the national enquiry facility through which the running position of trains is given to passengers.

q: Under the e-payment facility, an authorised freight customer does not hand over cash or a cheque at the goods booking office for the freight due from him. Instead, he pays the freight:

options.A: In cash at the goods booking office itself
options.B: By cheque handed over to the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.C: By money order sent to the destination station
options.D: Electronically through banks, the amount being credited directly to the Railway's account

e: Under e-payment, an authorised freight customer pays freight electronically through banks, the amount being credited directly to the Railway account, without cash or cheque at the booking office.

q: Under a liberalised scheme, freight customers were enabled to invest in wagons which the Railways then operated for their traffic. The abbreviation LWIS stands for:
e: LWIS stands for Liberalised Wagon Investment Scheme, under which freight customers invest in wagons which the Railways operate for their traffic.

q: A freight terminal developed by a private party for handling rail freight traffic is an important part of the freight marketing policy of Indian Railways. In this connection, the abbreviation PFT stands for:
e: PFT stands for Private Freight Terminal, a freight terminal developed by a private party for handling rail freight traffic under the freight marketing policy.

q: For traffic moving regularly between two specified stations, the Railways notify special concessional freight rates for that pair of stations instead of the general class rates. Such rates are known as:
e: Special concessional rates notified for traffic moving regularly between two specified stations, instead of the general class rates, are Station-to-Station or STS rates.

q: The Railways assure stable freight arrangements to their major freight customers who, in return, assure a minimum volume of traffic over a period. Such arrangements are made under:
e: Long Term Tariff Contracts are made with major freight customers who assure a minimum traffic volume over a period, in return for stable freight arrangements from the Railways.

q: To earn more revenue from sources other than fares and freight, the Railways invite new and innovative ideas from staff and the public. The scheme associated with generating such non-fare revenue is:
e: NINFRIS is the scheme for generating non-fare revenue by inviting new and innovative ideas from staff and the public for sources other than fares and freight.

q: When goods are accepted at a station for carriage by rail, the document issued to the consignor serves both as a receipt for the goods and as evidence of the contract of carriage between him and the Railways. This document is the:
e: The Railway Receipt is issued to the consignor on acceptance of goods. It is both the receipt for the goods and evidence of the contract of carriage with the Railways.

q: A consignee presents himself at the destination station to take delivery of his consignment. Delivery of the goods is normally given to him:

options.A: On a verbal request, without any document
options.B: Only after the expiry of the free time for removal
options.C: On surrender of the Railway Receipt by him or his endorsee
options.D: Only in the presence of the consignor

e: Goods are delivered at destination only against their authority document, namely on surrender of the Railway Receipt by the consignee or his endorsee.

q: A consignor is offered carriage of his goods at two different rates and chooses the rate at which the Railways' liability is limited. As compared with the railway risk rate, the freight charges at the owner's risk rate are:
e: At the owner risk rate the Railways liability is limited, so the freight charged is lower than at the railway risk rate, where the Railways bear the fuller risk.

q: A goods clerk has to work out the freight payable on a consignment offered for booking. Freight charges on goods traffic are determined mainly on the basis of:

options.A: The classification of the commodity and the distance over which it is carried, applied to the chargeable weight
options.B: The market value of the goods alone
options.C: The speed of the train by which the goods are carried
options.D: The number of wagons in the rake

e: Freight on goods is determined mainly by the classification of the commodity and the distance carried, applied to the chargeable weight of the consignment.

q: At a destination station, goods have arrived and been delivered, but the freight payable on them at destination has still not been collected from the consignees. In station accounts, this amount represents:

options.A: Freight deposited in advance by merchants
options.B: Refund of freight payable to merchants
options.D: Outstanding freight, being 'to-pay' freight not yet collected

e: To-pay freight on goods delivered but not yet collected from consignees is outstanding freight in station accounts, recoverable from them at destination.

q: On one consignment the freight is paid by the consignor at the time of booking, while on another it is left to be collected when the goods are delivered. In goods booking, the terms 'Paid' and 'To Pay' indicate:

options.A: Whether the freight is paid at the forwarding station or is to be collected at the destination
options.B: Whether payment is made in cash or by cheque
options.C: Whether the traffic is a full rake load or a piecemeal load
options.D: Whether the traffic is local or through traffic

e: In goods booking, Paid means freight is paid by the consignor at the forwarding station, and To Pay means it is to be collected from the consignee at destination.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A route kilometre is the length of line between two points, irrespective of the number of tracks laid on that length.
2. A track kilometre is worked out by counting each running line separately.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A route kilometre counts the length of line between two points once, irrespective of tracks, while a track kilometre counts each running line separately. Both statements are correct.

q: For statistical purposes, the distances travelled by individual passengers during a period are added together. The aggregate so obtained gives the:
e: Passenger kilometres are obtained by adding the distances travelled by individual passengers in a period, and measure the coaching output in statistics.

q: An operating officer wants a figure showing how intensively a section of line is being used for carrying goods traffic. The density of traffic on a section is expressed as:

options.A: The number of trains run per day
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre
options.D: Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day

e: Density of traffic on a section shows how intensively it is used and is expressed as Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre of the section.

q: To judge the average load actually hauled by goods trains over a period, an operating officer divides the Net Tonne Kilometres performed by the goods train kilometres run. The figure he obtains is the:

options.A: Average net load of goods trains

e: Dividing Net Tonne Kilometres performed by goods train kilometres run gives the average net load hauled by goods trains over the period.

q: A statement shows what proportion of the total wagon kilometres run by a railway was run by wagons carrying no load. The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres indicates:

options.A: The wagon turn-round of the railway
options.B: The average load carried by wagons
options.C: The fuel efficiency of goods working
options.D: The extent of empty (unloaded) running of wagons

e: The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres shows the extent of empty or unloaded running of wagons on the railway.

q: In passenger statistics, a distinction is drawn between passengers received from other railways and those who begin their rail journey on the home railway itself. 'Originating passengers' on a railway are those who:

options.A: Alight at stations of that railway
options.B: Commence their journey from stations on that railway
options.C: Are received from other railways at junctions

e: Originating passengers are those who commence their journey from stations on the home railway itself, as distinct from passengers received from other railways.

q: A statistics clerk is asked to prepare the monthly statement that deals exclusively with how passenger trains have performed on his railway. The statement he should compile is:
e: Monthly Statistical Statement 1 deals exclusively with passenger train performance, as distinct from Statement 2 which covers goods train performance.

q: In the monthly statistical series of Indian Railways, Statement 4-A is the statement that reports the performance of:
e: In the monthly statistical series, Statement 4-A reports the performance of rolling stock, namely locomotives, while carriages and wagons fall under 4-B.

q:
A statistics assistant is matching two monthly returns in the 5-series with their subject matter. Consider the following statements:
1. Statement 5-A of the monthly series is devoted to fuel and power statistics.
2. Statement 5-B of the monthly series is devoted to lubricating oil statistics.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 5-A covers fuel and power statistics and Statement 5-B covers lubricating oil statistics in the monthly series. Both statements are correct.

q: A suburban section compiler has to report the performance of the Electric Multiple Unit services run on his railway. The monthly statistical statement meant for this purpose is:
e: The performance of Electric Multiple Unit suburban services is reported in Monthly Statistical Statement 8 in the monthly statistical series.

q:
Two monthly statements in the 3-series are sometimes confused with each other. Consider the following statements:
1. Statement 3-A covers passenger and goods train performance, including tonne kilometres and the indices derived from them.
2. Statement 3-B gives details of through, van and shunting goods trains.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 3-A covers passenger and goods train performance with tonne kilometres and derived indices, and 3-B details through, van and shunting goods trains. Both are correct.

q: A factory owner proposes a private siding to his works and asks who will bear the entire cost of constructing it. The correct position is that the entire cost of construction of a private siding is borne by:

options.C: The Railways and the siding owner in equal shares

e: A private siding is constructed for the siding owner benefit, and the entire cost of its construction is borne by the siding owner, not by the Railways.

q: An eight-year-old child travels in a reserved coach with his parents and no separate berth is demanded for him. The fare chargeable for the child is:

options.B: No fare, as the child is carried free

e: A child of eight years, for whom no separate berth is demanded, is charged half fare. Full fare applies only if a separate berth is demanded for the child.

q: Before a handling bill rendered by a station is passed for payment, the Traffic Accounts Office checks it mainly with reference to:

options.A: The rates in the handling contract and the certified quantities of goods and parcels handled
options.B: The pay bills of the goods shed staff for the month
options.C: The total earnings of the station for the month
options.D: The number of wagons allotted to the station

e: A handling bill is checked in the Traffic Accounts Office mainly against the rates in the handling contract and the certified quantities of goods and parcels handled.

q: Licence fees recovered by the Railways for the bookstalls provided at stations are classified under:
e: Licence fees for bookstalls at stations are not coaching or goods earnings. They are classified under sundry other earnings of the Railways.

q: A parking contractor asks what happens to the security deposit he has lodged for his earning contract at a station. The correct position is that the deposit is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.B: Retained during the currency of the contract and refunded after its satisfactory completion and clearance of dues
options.C: Treated as a traffic earning of the station
options.D: Refunded on the very day the contract is awarded

e: A security deposit for an earning contract is retained during the currency of the contract and refunded after its satisfactory completion and clearance of all dues.

q: A goods clerk finds that the rate quoted for a customer's traffic between two named stations is lower than the ordinary class rate and is meant to hold that traffic against road competition. Such Station-to-Station rates are quoted by the Railways primarily in order to:

options.A: Attract and retain specified traffic between the nominated stations, particularly against road competition
options.B: Fix a uniform freight rate for all stations of the railway
options.C: Charge parcels moving between the nominated stations
options.D: Replace the Goods Tariff for all traffic

e: Station-to-Station rates are quoted primarily to attract and retain specified traffic between the nominated stations, particularly against road competition.

q:
A key freight customer who has entered into a Long Term Tariff Contract lists the benefits he expects from it. Consider the following statements:
1. He gets stability of freight rates for the period of the contract.
2. He earns incentives linked to the growth of traffic over the agreed level.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A Long Term Tariff Contract gives the customer stability of freight rates for the contract period and incentives linked to growth of traffic above the agreed level. Both are correct.

q: A private operator proposes to set up a freight terminal of his own for handling rail-borne traffic. A Private Freight Terminal of this kind is normally developed:

options.A: On railway land, entirely at the cost of the Railways
options.B: Within the circulating area of a passenger station
options.D: On private (non-railway) land by a private operator, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways

e: A Private Freight Terminal is normally developed on private, non-railway land by a private operator, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways.

q: A freight customer who is not the developer of a Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal asks whether he can use it for his traffic. The correct position is that such a terminal is:

options.A: Confined to the traffic of the developer alone
options.B: A common-user cargo terminal, open for handling the traffic of all freight customers
options.D: Provided only for the traffic of Government departments

e: A Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal is a common-user terminal. It is open for handling the traffic of all freight customers, not only its developer.

q: Under the Special Freight Train Operator scheme, the operator who has invested in special-purpose rakes is, in addition, required to:

options.A: Pay haulage charges to the Railways for the movement of his rakes over the railway network
options.B: Fix the freight rates for all customers of the Railways
options.C: Hand over his entire earnings to the Railways
options.D: Maintain the railway track used by his rakes

e: Under the Special Freight Train Operator scheme, the operator who invests in special-purpose rakes must also pay haulage charges to the Railways for moving his rakes.
